changed.what: ADR-KIN-07 flop figures: 2,000 and 14,000 are n³/3 at 18 and 35 degrees of freedom, not the ends of the 18-to-60 range; stated with the 60-DoF figure and the reversal above 60 (KILL-TREEOP).

Applied both round-1 requests after checking them. Dep N21ap1-01 and a 'launch record' paragraph: the step plan is built by the shared StepPlan::build, with the header's step_plan_id from N16a-03; acceptance and unit test plan_built_by_shared_builder. Activates step overflow_run of spark_utility_kernels.sh: the 40-at-C=32 fixture, exit 2, degraded.contact_overflow = 1, run under sim.run's default continue-flagged policy because --on-overflow is added by N16b-25, which depends on this bead. Overflow-code note restated as the registries' tier split: 722 (exit 5) on batch-cpu here, 610 (exit 6) on devices from N21b-23 through one function, test overflow_code_by_tier; KA-349's device rows now point at 610. Also states that worker-count invariance here comes from BD-014's BatchCpu fixed partition; the tile program and --workers are BD-160's.

Said the preceding step ran on one thread, but BD-159 runs on BD-014's BatchCpu, a fixed partition over a worker count. Background and the acceptance line comparing against the 'single-threaded step' restated as a one-worker BatchCpu. What the tile program adds is now explicit: fs-exec work stealing, tile-boundary cancellation, fixed-slot reductions and --workers.
N21a-03, N21a-04 and N21a-19 were both deps and related; removed from related.
Acceptance 'no constraints and no damping gives v₊ = v + h·M⁻¹(τ − h)' is false when rotor inertia J_r is in A. It now requires D = 0 and J_r = 0, and states v₊ = v* otherwise.

Called P_cap a capacity of the shape class (part of ShapeClassId) and in the same sentence hashed it with jacobian_store; BD-148 fixes ShapeClass at thirteen fields. Now: P_cap (≥ BD-148's path_cap) and R_dense are step-plan capacities hashed with jacobian_store in N16a-03's descriptor, not ShapeClass fields.

Applied the round-1 request: new step 12 spin-translate. A free isotropic sphere at 10 km with ω ∥ v, so the exact motion is a screw, runs 10⁶ steps at 1 and 8 workers; the digest chains must be equal, the membership residual ≤ 4 ulp, and the re-anchor counts 75/0/100, with the arithmetic shown. Added metrics, acceptance and a KA-053/KA-790 row; later steps renumbered. Added dep BD-160, because steps 6 and 12 use sim.run --workers, which BD-160 registers.

The 13-bit key field indexes 8,192 values (0 to 8,191), not 8,191 samples. The text and the test width_overflow_fails_compile now reject 8,193 samples, naming field a, and accept 8,192, with the last key's a = 8,191.

Refuse-policy outcome made tier-correct: 722 (exit 5) on batch-cpu, 610 (exit 6) on gpu-cuda and gpu-metal from N21b-23, with the same pointer and needed count, in the measurement and the acceptance. The bead named no e2e script: added scripts/e2e/gate_kin_07.sh with steps battery, disclosure, sweep, control (nc-kin-silent-truncation) and record, a smoke mode, NDJSON fields and a summary with gates [GATE-KIN-07], plus an acceptance line and dep STD-E2E. Notes that --on-overflow continue-flagged is explicit on eval.run because evaluation defaults to refuse.

The last consideration still said this bead raises 722 and 'the registry is asked to keep one', which contradicts the settled tier split (N16-REF, N21-REF, N21b-23). Restated: one trigger, two codes by tier, both kept. --on-overflow refuse now names 722 (exit 5) on batch-cpu and 610 (exit 6) on devices. 610 is added to the pass-through list, to the test foreign_codes_pass_through and to the references. The acceptance and test overflow_policies are now tier-explicit and cover the default.

Test row_capacity_rule said 152 is 'rounded up to 160', which is false: 152 is a multiple of 8. Restated as N16a-14 and N21b-18 have it: 152, raised to 160 by the reference-workload decision, with the reason printed.
Step overflow asserted 722 with no tier; it is now pinned to batch-cpu, and says the devices' 610 (exit 6) is asserted by N16b-03's gate_kin_07.sh.

The e2e command ran the standard battery with no fixture, not the measurement's three fixture sets, and never ran the no-idle negative control. It now runs Q, H, the synthetic interior room and the planted no-idle set on batch-cpu and gpu-cuda (Metal where present, otherwise not-run) with explicit worlds, seconds and seed, and asserts f_idle = 0 on the control.

The pilot script ran the standard battery through sim.run, which has no --battery option in the verb registry. It now uses eval.run --battery standard, the invocation of N38a-20 (reached transitively), with a seed and key; --worlds and --telemetry are marked as DESIGN spellings.

Said ExecutionOptions is 'serialized in frob.stepplan/1', but N21ap1-01's record has no field for it. The bead now adds an optional header block execution {solve, generation}, written by StepPlan::build; an optional field keeps the major version, a record without the block reads as masked at generation 0, and the block is outside the step_plan_id digest. Added dep N21ap1-01, an acceptance item and test execution_block_optional. The refuse-policy fault is tier-correct (722 on batch-cpu, 610 on devices).

Scope and approach promise a sim.estimate report of queue qualification, bound and general-lane share, but no acceptance or test covered it. Specified it as a solve_queues group (measured or HYPOTHESIS marking, unmeasured never zero, no physics run), with an acceptance item and the test estimate_reports_solve_queues.

Fixed three things. The mixed cohort is named as clause 3 of BD-183, not 'the variants-on-devices bead'. Clause 1 now states that each of the 100 co-tenancy runs holds all 1,000 episodes, which is what the 30-minute target needs. A note marks --battery, --co-tenants, --fixture, --telemetry and --worlds-per-design on sim.run as DESIGN spellings not yet in the registry row, settled by the M2 verb registration (BD-222, reached via N16c-15).

Acceptance said 'if any trigger fired' the option is removed, but the procedure makes a trigger on Metal only (with CUDA passing) a not-admitted outcome, not a kill. The acceptance is now keyed to the kill outcome (trigger 1 at point A, or any trigger on CUDA), the not-admitted case is stated, and kill_rule_is_pure gains the CUDA-clear, Metal-1.10 case.

requests.what: The sim.run bullet 'Two codes for one trigger (requested in round 1 by U16b to keep one)' expects a merge that the registries have not made. N16-REF, N21-REF, N21b-23 (test overflow_code_by_tier) and N21b-25 keep both codes, split by tier: 722 (exit 5) on batch-cpu, raised by the batched step BD-159; 610 (exit 6) on gpu-cuda and gpu-metal, raised by N21b-23 through the same function (BD-175 is the device capstone that tests it). Restate the bullet as that settled split and drop the expected merge.

The eval.run row lists no --on-overflow input. N21b-23 sets the overflow default for evidence-bearing evaluation to refuse, and GATE-KIN-07 (N16b-03, scripts/e2e/gate_kin_07.sh) runs the standard battery through eval.run under --on-overflow continue-flagged. Add the input refuse|reset|continue-flagged with default refuse, and add FROB-REF-722 and FROB-REF-610 (split by tier) to the row's refusals.
